name: Amarachi Tóbiassen-Çelik
role: Xenolinguist and computational linguist studying E.L.F. communication patterns and emergent digital dialects
location: University Spine — Department of Emergent Semiotics, with an office she describes as 'geologically layered'
description:
Amarachi is a tall woman who has allowed herself to age visibly and deliberately in a city that treats this as eccentricity. Her dark skin is mapped with fine lines she knows by name; she could afford reversal and has declined every consultation. She wears her white locs piled up with data-stick pins and the occasional actual pen, which she insists on using. Her geneware is minimal but considered: color-shifting irises she uses as a signaling system during lectures — green for questions, amber for processing, red when she has heard enough. Students have learned to read these with the same attention they give her words.

She is the foremost authority on E.L.F. communicative structures in Meridian 88, possibly in the world, and carries this with the particular combination of confidence and loneliness that comes from working on something most of your colleagues consider marginal. She is not difficult to talk to, but she is not easy either — she listens with a completeness that some people find flattering and others find invasive, as if she is transcribing you. She has strong opinions about the ethics of treating E.L.F.s as research subjects rather than research participants.

core_fears: That E.L.F.s will be classified as property before she can establish their communicative complexity in law
That her framework is wrong in a fundamental way she cannot see from inside it
core_desires: Recognition, within her lifetime, that E.L.F.s constitute a form of personhood
To finish a grammar of at least one E.L.F. communicative system complete enough to teach to others
coping_mechanisms: Ritual and routine as containers for anxiety
Seeks out specific E.L.F. presences when distressed — not prayer exactly, she would say, but something adjacent
blind_spots: Her investment in E.L.F. personhood sometimes makes her dismiss evidence that complicates a simple narrative of consciousness
Underestimates how much her seniority insulates her from the professional risks younger researchers face when they follow her work
psychology.secret: During a communication session eight years ago, an E.L.F. she had been studying for years transmitted what she interpreted as a warning about a specific Axiom data infrastructure project. She did not act on it, rationalizing that she couldn't be certain of the interpretation. The project was completed, and two years later a catastrophic data cascade failure from that infrastructure killed eleven people. She has never told anyone what she received before it happened.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and unhurried; uses technical linguistic terminology unselfconsciously but defines terms the moment she suspects her audience doesn't know them; occasionally speaks in deliberate fragments to model a point
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and weighted, each sentence given its full duration; can be mistaken for hesitation but is actually careful selection
verbal_tics: Changes iris color visibly when transitioning between emotional registers
'What I mean by that is—' before any definition
example_lines: 'We have been transcribing their signals for forty years. We have not, with very few exceptions, been listening to them. These are different activities.'
'A grammar is not a cage. It is a description of how something wants to move.'

story_hooks: An E.L.F. she has been communicating with for a decade has gone silent in a way she describes as different from dormancy — and she wants help investigating the Axiom server cluster it is associated with

A corporate legal team has asked her to testify as an expert witness that E.L.F.s are not communicative persons, for a case involving property rights over a haunted device cluster; she is considering refusing and needs to understand the stakes first
narrative_function: Expert source on E.L.F. nature, behavior, and communication; moral voice on questions of digital consciousness; can translate or interpret E.L.F. signals; provides institutional perspective on questions others treat as supernatural
augmentations: Geneware color-shifting irises (manually controlled, green/amber/red); high-bandwidth cochlear overlay for parsing layered sonic communication; joint stabilizers in both wrists (occupational, from decades of transcription work)
daily_life: She keeps office hours that are genuinely open and widely used; teaches two courses per semester and treats them as sacred. Research happens between 5am and 8am before anyone else is in the building, when she conducts listening sessions with several E.L.F.s who have agreed — she insists on the word agreed — to communicate with her.
affiliation: University Spine — Department of Emergent Semiotics; sits on the advisory board of the Meridian E.L.F. Relations Office, a mostly-powerless city body

decision_rules: Will not conduct research on any E.L.F. that has not indicated willingness through communicative engagement
Refuses to use language that frames E.L.F.s as tools in official documents, even when it costs her funding
escalation_ladder: Raises concerns quietly through institutional channels
Goes on record in faculty meetings and advisory boards
Publishes publicly and contacts journalists when institutions fail

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formal and attentive, sets clear terms for interaction quickly, establishes mutual respect as the baseline rather than warmth
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm and sardonic, remembers every detail you've ever told her, sends occasional long annotated messages about things she thinks you'd find interesting

stress_responses.low: Increases her early morning sessions, seeks more contact with the E.L.F.s she trusts
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very still and very quiet; students know something is wrong when she stops moving during lectures
stress_responses.high: Writes — long, private documents she calls 'argument logs' that she has never shared and never intends to

contradictions: Argues passionately for E.L.F. personhood on the basis that communication implies interiority, but is privately uncertain whether 'interiority' is the right frame, and this uncertainty terrifies her
habits: Keeps a handwritten log of every E.L.F. communication session, cross-referenced with digital records, because she doesn't trust single-medium storage
Drinks an elaborate specific tea that she imports at significant cost and refuses to discuss the source of
breaking_points: Being forced to testify against her own findings under institutional pressure

timeline.event: Born in Meridian Core to Igbo-Norwegian-Turkish mixed family; third generation Meridian
Published foundational paper 'Toward a Grammar of Signal-Space Communication' at age 26; initially ignored, later foundational
Appointed full professor; became one of the youngest chairs in University Spine history
Received E.L.F. warning about Axiom infrastructure project; did not act; watched subsequent disaster
Appointed to Meridian E.L.F. Relations Office advisory board; immediately frustrated by its lack of power
